solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rascal set off for the OTC

definitions.note: the Officers' Training Corps, whose members are trainees; the definition stands for its members

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable rascal

indicators.note: set off here means jolted out of place, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rogue heads off to join the university officer-training unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' looks like 'departed', but 'off' is the anagram signal. The OTC is the Officers' Training Corps, a British university military training body.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a training corps for officers are trainees in uniform, known collectively as cadets.

clue.text: Clergyman has tea with Frank

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea
frank means plain-spoken, so plain

explanation.surface: A vicar takes tea with a man called Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman attached to an institution such as a college, hospital or regiment is its chaplain.

clue.text: Neighbourhood detective's scrupulous

parts.note: read as 'detective is': DI, a Detective Inspector, with the 's as a linking verb
scrupulous means strict, exacting

explanation.surface: The local police officer is careful about everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbourhood is an area or locality, a synonym for a district.

clue.text: Acting award for knight in play

indicators.note: the knight is placed in the word for play, so N sits inside

parts.note: to play with something is to toy with it
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An actor in a play wins a theatre prize for portraying a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside TOY. The Tony is the American theatre award.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony Award honours achievement in Broadway theatre, including stage acting.

clue.text: Is in Paris holding shipment of delicacy

indicators.note: the French word grips the shipment within it, so it goes around

parts.note: est is French for is
a cargo is a shipment of goods

explanation.surface: In Paris a consignment of a fine food is being kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is in Paris' asks for the French word for 'is'; 'holding' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails cooked in garlic butter are a celebrated French delicacy served under that name.

clue.text: Support heavyweight ace? That's matchless!

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
a ton is a heavy weight
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: Backing a champion heavyweight boxer, a fan declares him unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavyweight' looks like a boxer, but it is the weight TON; 'That's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning the best of all, beaten by nobody, so without equal or matchless.

clue.text: Sales manager organised a nice route

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sales manager plans a pleasant travel route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges the letters of A NICE ROUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who runs a sale at auction, taking bids, is cheekily called a sales manager.

clue.text: Poet's ego disturbed by article

definitions.note: read as 'Poet is', the noun with a linking verb

indicators.note: by means next to, placing one piece beside the other
disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of ego are jumbled

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A writer's self-image is shaken by a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns EGO into GOE; 'by' sets THE beside it. 'Poet's' is read as 'poet is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was the great German poet and dramatist who wrote Faust.

clue.text: Most boring amateur seen during exam

indicators.note: the amateur is seen in the middle of the exam, so placed within it

parts.note: an exam is a test
AM is a standard abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: The dullest amateur turns up in the middle of a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely bland and unexciting is the most tame, a superlative meaning dullest.

clue.text: Agree condition at the time of despatch

definitions.meaning: to agree to something is to give consent

definitions.text: condition at the time of despatch
definitions.meaning: split into two short words meaning in the state in which goods were posted

explanation.surface: Two parties agree on the state of goods when shipped.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into AS SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal agreement, and split in two it describes goods in the state they were posted.

clue.text: Rice came cooked in dessert

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rice was prepared and served in a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges RICE CAME; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen sweet made from dairy is a popular dessert.

clue.text: Produce system giving a better game

definitions.note: a better is one who bets, so a gambler's game

parts.note: fruit is produce from a garden or farm
a machine is a system or organisation

explanation.surface: A farming setup yields an improved sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'improved', but it is one who bets. A fruit machine is the British name for a slot machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot machine with spinning reels of cherries and lemons is a gambling game for a punter.

clue.text: Entice student to the river

indicators.note: to here means attached to, placing the river after the student

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Tempt a student down to the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from British learner-driver plates; the Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure is to tempt or draw someone in, a straight synonym for entice.

clue.text: Displays cereal bowls

parts.note: bran is the husk of cereal grain
bowls are dishes

explanation.surface: A shop window shows breakfast cereal in bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowls' looks like a verb, but it is the plural noun for dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or wave something about for show is to exhibit it, so displays.

clue.text: Popular Dutch sealant for consideration

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
cement is used to seal joints

explanation.surface: A well-liked Dutch filler is under consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: In law and business, a consideration is a payment or incentive offered to persuade someone.

clue.text: Determined to keep prisoner blowing hot and cold

indicators.note: the determined word keeps the prisoner held inside it

parts.note: insistent means determined, demanding
con is short for convict

explanation.surface: A resolute jailer holds an inmate whose mood keeps changing.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for vacillating, swinging between enthusiasm and indifference, so erratic and changeable.

clue.text: Terrier publicised beer

parts.note: aired means broadcast or made public
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A dog promoted a brand of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'publicised' sounds like a homophone signal but is the synonym AIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is the largest breed of terrier, named after a Yorkshire valley.

clue.text: Bomb factory of vegetable producer

parts.note: egg is old slang for a bomb or grenade
a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: A munitions works also grows vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links. 'Egg' as slang for a bomb comes from RAF usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine is the vegetable, and the plant that bears it shares the American name.

clue.text: Tenor appears in mocking novel

indicators.note: the tenor turns up inside the mocking word, so it is placed within

parts.note: guying means ridiculing or mocking
tenor means general manner or character

explanation.surface: A singer features in a satirical book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' looks like a singer, but it means the general drift or character of something; 'appears in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Mannering is an 1815 historical romance by Sir Walter Scott.

clue.text: Girl making concession having to hurry

parts.note: a sop is a concession to placate someone
hie is an archaic word meaning to hurry

explanation.surface: A girl gives way because she has to rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' and 'having' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophie is a common female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Dramatist introduces a monarch to cheese

indicators.note: the cheese takes in the other letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A playwright presents a king with some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduces' puts A and R inside BRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish playwright who created Peter Pan.

clue.text: Sparkling drink gets fragrance after a little work

indicators.note: the drink and fragrance come after the little work in the answer

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
ale is a drink
a scent is a fragrance

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink acquires a perfume after a short job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' links; OP is the abbreviation of opus.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing a shimmering play of colours like an opal is a kind of sparkling, iridescent look.

clue.text: Look over castle

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: to peek is to look quickly

explanation.surface: Survey a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look over' wants to be a phrase meaning inspect; 'over' turns PEEK around.
explanation.definitionFit: The keep is the strongest central tower of a medieval fortress, so part of a castle.

clue.text: Tell stories about lots of parasites

indicators.note: the lies go round the letter for lots, so it sits inside

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. lots

explanation.surface: Gossip about plenty of bloodsuckers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C inside LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Small wingless insects living on hair and skin are a familiar example of parasites.

clue.text: Dissident keeps motorway sealed

indicators.note: the dissident holds the motorway inside, so it goes within

parts.note: a heretic dissents from orthodoxy
M is the British road letter for a motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A rebel blocks a motorway, closing it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts M inside HERETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermetic means airtight, closed so completely that nothing can pass.

clue.text: Scoundrel in spy organisation is a six-footer

indicators.note: the scoundrel is placed in the spy organisation

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a cad is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rogue in the intelligence service turns out to be very tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it means an insect with six legs. 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so a chirping insect of the trees is a six-footer.

clue.text: Despite that has affair with bird

parts.note: an affair is an event or occasion
a hen is a bird, joined on after

explanation.surface: Despite that, someone has a fling with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests a romance; here it is an occasion. 'bird' is British slang for a woman in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase meaning nevertheless, conceding a point while still holding firm.

clue.text: Church set in a hollow is respectable

indicators.note: the church is set inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church built in a valley is a reputable one.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent means proper and of good standing, a synonym for respectable.
